question.problem:
Calculate 
${\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }\frac{8}{{n}^{2}+6n+8}.$

*Hint: Try to factor the denominator first.*
question.worked_solution:
First, note that the series can be written as

$$
8{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{2}+6n+8}.
$$

We can factor the denominator and use partial fractions to show that

$$
\frac{1}{{n}^{2}+6n+8}=\frac{1}{(n+2)(n+4)}=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+2}-\frac{1}{n+4}).
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
8{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+2}-\frac{1}{n+4})=4{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n+2}-\frac{1}{n+4}).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{2} & =4[(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6})] \\ {s}_{3} & =4[(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6})+(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7})] \\ {s}_{4} & =4[(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{8})] \\ {s}_{5} & =4[(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\frac{1}{5}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\frac{1}{8})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{9})] \\ {s}_{6} & =4[(\frac{1}{4}-\cancel{\frac{1}{6}})+(\frac{1}{5}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{6}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{8}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{9})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{8}}-\frac{1}{10})]\end{aligned}
$$

We notice that all of the terms cancel except $\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{5},$ and the $-\frac{1}{N+3}$ and  $-\frac{1}{N+4}$ terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
{s}_{N}=4[\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{N+3}-\frac{1}{N+4}].
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }\frac{8}{{n}^{2}+6n+8} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }⁡{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }⁡4[\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{N+3}-\frac{1}{N+4}] \\  & =4{lim}_{N\to \infty }⁡[\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{N+3}-\frac{1}{N+4}] \\  & =4[\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{5}-0-0] \\  & =4[\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{5}] \\  & =4\cdot \frac{9}{20} \\  & =\frac{9}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
